title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a near-empty divider or heading sheet. In the top right, in pencil, it reads: 'Descriptions transcendantes de motifs en car. 0 et de catégories de motifs en car. 0' (transcendental descriptions of motives in characteristic 0 and of categories of motives in characteristic 0). Below a blue ink rule it reads 'doubles réseaux etc' (double lattices, etc.). Two small ink sketches follow: (1) an open-bottomed bracket ⊓ with paired short vertical strokes at its left-lower and right-upper ends; (2) a ⊏-shaped open rectangle. The number 20 is at the bottom.

The page sits right after a 1965 English letter, probably to Mumford, given the reference to 'your Boulder talk'; this is presumably Mumford's 'Families of abelian varieties', Boulder 1965. That letter discusses when quotients V/Γ of period domains, with their variations of Hodge structure, are algebraic, conditionally on the Hodge and Tate conjectures.

In modern language, the heading announces a programme: describe the category of motives over a characteristic-0 field (say a subfield K of C) by transcendental, linear-algebra data. The likely data is a Betti realization (a finite-dimensional Q-space, or Z-lattice) together with a de Rham realization (a K-space with Hodge filtration) and a comparison isomorphism after tensoring with C. 'Doubles réseaux' (double lattices) plausibly means such a pair of rational structures in a single complex vector space: a Q-lattice and a K-structure. The 'periods' are the matrix relating them. For K = C alone, this reduces to a polarizable Q-Hodge structure; the sketches may be schematic notation for such pairs. Then 'categories of motives' would be realized as subcategories of such linear-algebra categories, through the Hodge (or Betti plus de Rham) realization functor. That is how one gets the motivic Galois group as the Mumford–Tate group, or its K-analogue.

The page states no result. It only names a topic, whose development presumably follows on later pages (the next page's transcription is only '21').
errors: No mathematical assertions, so nothing to check. The meaning of 'doubles réseaux' and of the sketches is an interpretation, not certain.

ideas.what: Describe motives and categories of motives in characteristic 0 transcendentally, via realization functors into linear-algebra categories (Hodge structures, Betti plus de Rham with comparison).
ideas.modern_name: Hodge / Betti–de Rham realizations; system of realizations; Mumford–Tate group as motivic Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letters to Serre 1964, standard conjectures programme); developed by Deligne (Hodge II, 1971; Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih LNM 900, 1982; 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes', 1979); Jannsen (mixed realizations, 1990)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck–Serre correspondence (1964 letters on motives); Récoltes et Semailles mentions motives and the motivic Galois group in general terms

ideas.what: 'Doubles réseaux': plausibly a pair of rational structures (Q-Betti lattice and K-de Rham structure) in one complex space, i.e. a period structure.
ideas.modern_name: Period structure / Betti–de Rham comparison; period matrices; related to the Grothendieck period conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', Publ. IHÉS 29, 1966); Deligne 1979; André
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck 1966, IHÉS 29 (footnote on periods), if the interpretation is right

missed.claim: A heading planning a transcendental (Hodge-theoretic / period-lattice) description of motives and of whole categories of motives in characteristic 0, under the label 'doubles réseaux'. If 'double lattices' means Betti plus de Rham rational structures, it is an early (1965) trace of the realization or period viewpoint later systematized by Deligne and Jannsen. The page itself contains no development.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It could help date when Grothendieck tied the motivic Galois group to Hodge and period data, near the Mumford letter on Mumford–Tate-type questions. The mathematical content itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is only a heading with two unexplained sketches. The theme (transcendental realizations of motives, Mumford–Tate as motivic Galois group, periods) is well known and attributed to Grothendieck and Deligne. The phrase 'doubles réseaux' is a mildly interesting early label, but carries no content on this page.
